concepts.name: WTO's Foundational Architecture: From GATT to WTO
key_dimensions: Key structural differences between GATT (1947) and WTO (1995) — legal personality, membership, scope
Marrakesh Agreement (1994) as the founding treaty and its binding nature on all members
Why GATT was a 'provisional agreement' while WTO is a permanent international organization
UPSC trap: GATT still exists as GATT 1994 (goods) within the WTO framework — it was not abolished

concepts.name: Core Principles of WTO: MFN, National Treatment, and Their Exceptions
key_dimensions: Most Favoured Nation (MFN) under GATT Article I vs. GATS Article II vs. TRIPS Article 4 — different scope and exceptions
National Treatment principle (GATT Article III) — applies only after goods enter the market, not at border
Critical exceptions: Regional Trade Agreements (Article XXIV), Generalized System of Preferences (GSP), and developing country waivers
UPSC trap: MFN does not mean 'most favourable' treatment to all — it means equal treatment; and GSP is a legally-sanctioned deviation from MFN

concepts.name: WTO Agreements Architecture: Goods, Services, and Intellectual Property
key_dimensions: Three pillars: GATT 1994 (goods), GATS (services), TRIPS (intellectual property) — binding on all members
Plurilateral vs. Multilateral agreements within WTO — only some members bound by plurilaterals (e.g., Government Procurement Agreement)
Single Undertaking principle — members must accept all agreements as a package (with plurilateral exceptions)
UPSC trap: Not all WTO agreements are binding on all members — plurilateral agreements are the exception

concepts.name: GATS: General Agreement on Trade in Services — Modes of Supply
key_dimensions: Four modes: Cross-border supply (Mode 1), Consumption abroad (Mode 2), Commercial presence (Mode 3), Movement of natural persons (Mode 4)
India's strategic interest in Mode 4 (IT/ITES professionals) and Mode 1 (software exports)
Positive list approach in GATS — members only commit to sectors they voluntarily schedule (unlike GATT's negative list approach)
UPSC trap: GATS covers services but explicitly excludes services supplied in the exercise of governmental authority

concepts.name: TRIPS Agreement: Minimum Standards and Flexibilities
key_dimensions: TRIPS sets minimum standards for patents (20 years), copyrights, trademarks, geographical indications — not maximum standards
Doha Declaration on TRIPS and Public Health (2001) — compulsory licensing, parallel imports as flexibilities
India's position: Section 3(d) of Patents Act (evergreening prevention) and its compatibility with TRIPS
UPSC trap: TRIPS-plus provisions in bilateral FTAs go beyond WTO TRIPS minimums — a key controversy for developing countries

concepts.name: WTO Dispute Settlement Mechanism (DSM): Structure and Crisis
key_dimensions: Three-tier process: Consultations → Panel → Appellate Body (AB) — with strict timelines
Appellate Body crisis: USA blocking AB member appointments since 2017 rendering AB non-functional from December 2019
Multi-Party Interim Appeal Arbitration Arrangement (MPIA) as a workaround — India is a participant
UPSC trap: WTO DSM rulings are binding and can authorize retaliation (cross-retaliation), unlike most international bodies — making it uniquely powerful

concepts.name: Agreement on Agriculture (AoA): Three Pillars and India's Concerns
key_dimensions: Three pillars: Market Access (tariff reduction), Domestic Support (Aggregate Measurement of Support — AMS), Export Subsidies
Green Box (minimally trade-distorting), Blue Box (production-limiting), Amber Box (trade-distorting) subsidies classification
India's food security concern: Public Stockholding (PSH) for food security programs and the 10% AMS cap issue
Bali Peace Clause (2013) and Nairobi Decision (2015) — interim shield for developing countries on PSH pending permanent solution

concepts.name: Public Stockholding (PSH) for Food Security: India's Negotiating Position
key_dimensions: The 10% de minimis limit on Amber Box support calculated on 1986-88 base prices — structurally disadvantageous to developing countries
India's demand for a permanent solution to PSH at WTO — Bali (2013) Peace Clause as temporary measure
G-33 coalition led by India vs. developed country resistance (USA, EU, Australia)
UPSC trap: The Peace Clause protects India from legal challenge but does NOT change the 10% rule — it is a moratorium, not a solution

concepts.name: Special and Differential Treatment (S&DT) for Developing Countries
key_dimensions: S&DT provisions: Longer implementation periods, technical assistance, less than full reciprocity in negotiations
Developed countries' push to graduate large emerging economies (India, China, Brazil) out of S&DT status — 'self-designation' controversy
Enabling Clause (1979) as the legal basis for GSP and developing country preferences
UPSC trap: There is no formal WTO definition of 'developing country' — members self-designate, which is a persistent source of conflict

concepts.name: WTO Ministerial Conferences: Key Outcomes and Failed Rounds
key_dimensions: Doha Development Round (2001) — launched but effectively stalled; development agenda vs. developed country interests
Cancún (2003) failure — Singapore Issues (investment, competition, procurement, trade facilitation) and developing country walkout
Bali (MC9, 2013) — Trade Facilitation Agreement (TFA) as first multilateral deal since WTO's founding
MC12 (Geneva, 2022) outcomes: TRIPS waiver for COVID vaccines (partial), fisheries subsidies agreement, food security exemptions

concepts.name: Trade Facilitation Agreement (TFA): Significance and Implementation
key_dimensions: First multilateral agreement concluded under WTO (2013, entered into force 2017) — historic significance
Three categories: Category A (immediate), B (with transition period), C (with capacity building support) — developing country flexibility
Estimated reduction in trade costs by 14.3% (WTO estimate) — key for MSME and developing country exporters
India's implementation: Single Window, customs modernization, and UPSC angle on Trade Facilitation Index

concepts.name: Fisheries Subsidies Agreement (2022): Provisions and India's Stand
key_dimensions: Prohibits subsidies for illegal, unreported, unregulated (IUU) fishing and overfished stocks
Developing country exemption: 25-year grace period for subsidies to fishing within Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ)
India's concern: Subsidy support to small and artisanal fishermen and fuel subsidies potentially covered
UPSC trap: This is the second substantive multilateral deal at WTO (after TFA) — often confused in sequencing questions

concepts.name: Anti-Dumping, Countervailing Duties, and Safeguards: WTO Rules
key_dimensions: Anti-dumping (GATT Article VI + Anti-Dumping Agreement): Action against below-cost exports — most frequently used trade remedy
Countervailing Duties (SCM Agreement): Against foreign government subsidies — requires injury determination
Safeguard measures (Article XIX + Safeguards Agreement): Temporary import restrictions due to surge — must be non-discriminatory (MFN-consistent)
UPSC trap: Safeguard measures apply to all countries equally (MFN), but anti-dumping and CVDs are country-specific — a critical distinction

concepts.name: GATT Article XX: General Exceptions and Environmental/Health Nexus
key_dimensions: Key exceptions: Protection of public morals (a), human/animal/plant life or health (b), conservation of exhaustible natural resources (g)
Two-tier test: Measure must fall under a listed exception AND comply with the Chapeau (not arbitrary/unjustifiable discrimination)
India's use: Quantitative restrictions on BOP grounds (Article XVIII:B) vs. Article XX — different legal basis
UPSC trap: Article XX does not provide blanket exceptions — the Chapeau condition is equally important and is where most cases are lost

concepts.name: WTO and Regional Trade Agreements (RTAs): The Spaghetti Bowl Problem
key_dimensions: GATT Article XXIV (goods) and GATS Article V (services) allow RTAs as exceptions to MFN — conditions: substantially all trade covered, tariffs not raised on outsiders
Proliferation of RTAs creating 'Spaghetti Bowl' effect — overlapping rules of origin undermining multilateralism
Transparency Mechanism for RTAs (2006) — notification and review requirement at WTO
India's selective FTA strategy vs. WTO multilateralism — RCEP withdrawal as a case study

concepts.name: WTO and Climate Change: Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) Controversy
key_dimensions: EU's CBAM — carbon tax on imports from countries with lower carbon pricing — WTO compatibility question under Article XX(b)/(g) and non-discrimination
Developing countries' (including India's) argument: CBAM is disguised protectionism and violates Common But Differentiated Responsibilities (CBDR)
WTO DSM has no explicit climate mandate — tension between trade rules and Paris Agreement obligations
UPSC angle: CBAM intersects Economy (trade), Environment (climate), and International Relations (India-EU) — a high-value cross-cutting issue

concepts.name: Geographical Indications (GIs) Under TRIPS and WTO Negotiations
key_dimensions: TRIPS Article 22-24: GI protection for all products (basic) vs. enhanced protection only for wines and spirits — developing country demand for extension
India's demand: Extension of higher-level TRIPS GI protection to agricultural products (Basmati, Darjeeling tea) and handicrafts
Basmati rice GI dispute — India vs. Pakistan — and WTO's role in bilateral trade disputes
UPSC trap: Under TRIPS, wines and spirits get stronger GI protection than all other products — this asymmetry is a major negotiating issue for India

concepts.name: E-Commerce Moratorium and Digital Trade at WTO
key_dimensions: 1998 WTO Moratorium on customs duties on electronic transmissions — renewed at every Ministerial Conference since then
Developing country concern: Revenue loss from not taxing digital trade; India and South Africa opposing permanent moratorium
Joint Statement Initiative (JSI) on E-commerce — plurilateral negotiations outside main WTO framework — India not a participant
UPSC trap: The moratorium is on customs duties only — it does NOT prevent domestic taxes (GST/VAT) on digital services; India's equalization levy is a separate matter

concepts.name: WTO's Institutional Structure: Decision-Making and the Consensus Problem
key_dimensions: WTO decisions by consensus — one member, one vote in principle, but consensus requirement gives de facto veto to any member
Ministerial Conference (highest body, every 2 years) → General Council → Subsidiary Councils (Goods, Services, TRIPS)
Critical Masses Agreement and Plurilateral approaches as alternatives when consensus fails
UPSC trap: WTO voting rules technically allow majority voting, but it has virtually never been used — consensus is the operational norm, making it both democratic and paralysis-prone

concepts.name: India's Strategic Positioning at WTO: Key Coalitions and Interests
key_dimensions: Key coalitions: G-33 (food security/PSH), G-20 developing (agricultural reform), NAMA-11 (industrial tariffs), Like-Minded Group
Offensive interests: Services (Mode 4), IT/ITES, generic pharmaceuticals (TRIPS flexibilities), GI extension
Defensive interests: Agriculture (PSH, food security), industrial policy space, e-commerce moratorium opposition
UPSC trap: India's G-20 at WTO is NOT the same as the G-20 Leaders' Summit (G20) — the WTO G-20 is a developing country coalition focused on agricultural reform
